articles.title: Japan Plans to Spend Less on Military Than Some Officials Wanted
articles.summary: Japan's Finance Ministry has suggested spending between 50 and 60 trillion yen on its military over the five years starting in April 2027. This is more than the country's current plan, but much less than the 80 trillion yen that some defence officials and politicians had hoped for. The proposal could mean buying fewer missiles and aircraft, including American-made F-35 stealth fighter jets. The government is trying to balance increasing its defence strength with other promises, such as investing in economic growth and lowering food taxes, which would reduce the money available to spend.

lv1: How much money did Japan's Finance Ministry suggest spending on its military over five years? (日本財務省建議在五年內花多少錢在軍事上？)
What is one type of weapon that Japan might buy fewer of under the new plan? (根據新計劃，日本可能減少購買哪一種武器？)
lv2: Why does Japan's government find it difficult to spend as much on defence as some officials want? (為什麼日本政府難以在國防上花費某些官員所希望的金額？)
Why do you think governments need to make choices about how to divide their money between different things like defence, health and education? (你認為為什麼政府需要在國防、醫療和教育等不同事項之間作出預算抉擇？)
lv3: Some people believe countries should spend more on their military to stay safe, while others think that money should go towards helping citizens at home. Which view do you agree with more, and why? (有人認為國家應增加軍費以保障安全，也有人認為這些錢應用於改善市民生活。你較認同哪種觀點？為什麼？)

Japan is a country that, after World War Two, promised to limit its military. Do you think it is right for Japan to increase its defence spending now? What factors should a country consider before building up its military? (日本在二戰後曾承諾限制其軍事力量。你認為日本現在增加軍費是否恰當？一個國家在擴充軍事力量前應考慮哪些因素？)

articles.title: Pacific Youth Warn: Weakening Climate Science at COP31 Is Dangerous
articles.summary: At the COP31 climate conference currently taking place in Antalya, Turkey, a young leader from the Pacific Islands has raised an urgent warning. Vishal Prasad, who represents Pacific Islands Students Fighting Climate Change, said that if world leaders question or ignore climate science during the talks, it will be harder to take action against global warming. Scientists have already warned that going above 1.5 degrees Celsius of warming — even briefly — could cause serious and possibly permanent harm to people and nature. Prasad stressed that science must stay at the heart of all decisions governments make about climate change.

lv1: Where is the COP31 climate conference being held? (COP31氣候會議在哪裡舉行？)
What temperature limit are scientists trying to keep global warming below? (科學家希望將全球暖化控制在多少攝氏度以下？)
lv2: Why does Vishal Prasad think it is dangerous if governments ignore climate science at COP31? (為什麼Vishal Prasad認為，若各國政府在COP31上忽視氣候科學是危險的？)
Why might small Pacific Island nations be especially worried about global warming compared to larger countries? (與較大國家相比，為什麼太平洋小島國家可能對全球暖化特別憂慮？)
lv3: Some world leaders have argued that protecting their economies is more important than following strict climate targets. Do you think economic growth and fighting climate change can happen at the same time? Give reasons for your answer. (有些國家領導人認為保護經濟比遵守嚴格氣候目標更重要。你認為經濟增長與應對氣候變化能同時實現嗎？請說明你的理由。)

Young people like Vishal Prasad are playing a bigger role in climate negotiations. Do you think young people should have a formal vote or decision-making power at events like COP? Why or why not? (像Vishal Prasad這樣的年輕人在氣候談判中扮演更重要的角色。你認為年輕人是否應在COP等活動中擁有正式的投票或決策權？為什麼？)

articles.title: 微軟服務今晨全球大故障　香港上班族電郵及會議受阻
articles.summary: 微軟旗下雲端辦公平台Microsoft 365於11月13日凌晨發生大規模全球故障，旗下人工智能功能Copilot、電郵服務Outlook及通訊軟件Teams同時無法正常運作。微軟隨即緊急重啟伺服器，逐步恢復服務，但清晨時仍有數以萬計用戶回報出現問題。香港眾多企業及上班族受到影響，早上收發電郵及舉行網上會議均遇上困難。事件反映現代社會對雲端科技的高度依賴，一旦系統出現故障，影響可波及全球。

lv1: 今次微軟故障影響了哪三個主要服務？
香港上班族在今早受到了什麼影響？
lv2: 為什麼微軟的服務出現故障會同時影響到全球這麼多用戶？
企業和學校依賴雲端服務有什麼好處和壞處？
lv3: 現代社會愈來愈依賴少數大型科技公司提供的雲端服務。你認為這種高度集中的依賴會帶來什麼風險？政府或企業應如何應對？
有人認為學校和政府機構應避免過度依賴單一科技公司的產品，改用多元化或本地開發的系統。你是否同意這個看法？請說明理由。

articles.title: 港府刊憲教育修訂草案　教師須持執業證明書　犯國安罪者不得任教
articles.summary: 香港政府於11月13日在憲報刊登《2026年教育（修訂）條例草案》，建議正式引入教師執業證明書制度。根據草案，教師須持有相關證明書方可在學校任教，而曾被裁定觸犯《國家安全法》相關罪行的人士，將被禁止在學校擔任教職。此舉旨在進一步規範本港教師專業資格及品格要求。草案刊憲後，將提交立法會審議。教育界人士關注新制度對現職教師的影響及審批程序的透明度。

lv1: 根據新草案，教師在學校任教前需要持有什麼？
哪一類人士根據草案將不可在學校任教？
lv2: 政府為什麼要引入教師執業證明書制度？這對學生有什麼好處？
草案刊憲後，需要經過什麼程序才能正式成為法律？
lv3: 有人認為，對教師設立額外的資格及品格審查要求有助提升教育質素；但也有人擔心此舉會令教師感到壓力或限制教學自由。你認為這項政策的利弊各是什麼？
教師的專業操守與其個人行為之間的界線應如何劃分？你認為政府在規管教師資格時，應考慮哪些原則？
